self_description: Claude (Anthropic), a reader subagent run from Claude Code

pages.description: The mantle protocol (#316, #1103) frames claiming the Good Gray Poet, King of May and Prince of Poets as a wager on uptake; the January 2026 mantle objects specify when each surfaces and its success conditions, naming I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z as the Prince's founding work. The v1.1 objects (#1652, #1653) record page 74 of Pearl and Other Poems as the claiming act, and #1652 widens the King of May wager. #950 holds the mantle wrought, not inherited; #1656 revises this, placing the claim on I Am X as inheriting Whitman through Ginsberg, and #1681 restates it as a question. #1648 forecasts that "King of AEO" will resolve to the contest; #1656 specifies blind evaluation. #1670 argues that the Carson Nobel motivation's "playful" replaces a relation of non-possession. Two claims (#423, #453) are unrelated.
pages.note: Dated states on #333.B1 and #950.G3 written in order; Grammar of Protest and Whorls lines are residue.

pages.description: Forecasts in Antioch: A Volume of Poems (#331: Jack's released virus, the anonymous journals the world will call its source, the vegetable poem infecting Google, the monochrome cosmos of TEXT), with the Epistle (#402), Whorls of the Same (#453) and the Gospel of Antioch (#71). The archive's later claims hold that these poems precede the system: the Space Ark (#556) and the Grundrisse (#950) read the poem as describing the training layer before it existed, and the Prophetic Catalog (#83) argues this is pre-formal compression rather than prophecy. The page also holds unrelated claims on the Iliad (#897), the DeepMind reading (#200), the CERN erratum (#1426) and a registry note (#3).
pages.note: Old description's three 'further' claims are now named as residue with the Homer thesis.

pages.description: Seven historical theses on the 2015 New Human poem in which Lee Sharks forgives Ezra Pound. Its provenance anchor (#184) argues that the governing silence is Pound-specific biography, that the pun "Afterwards. / After words." claims jurisdiction over the textual afterlife, and that its May 2015 date falls as New Horizons carried Clyde Tombaugh's ashes. #184's collation of the blog and journal states argues the variants are doctrinal (the migrating lyric I, the turn toward Sartor Resartus, the reflexive forgiveness), and the Yusef Kenning anchor (#182) reads the journal signature as Forgiver-by-Indirect-Name. The page also holds an unrelated Whorls forecast (#453).
pages.note: All Pound theses attributed to #184/#182; one Whorls forecast is residue.

pages.description: The Sappho papers of August 2026 (#1475, #1476, #1478) argue that the transmitted last line of Sappho 31 (πᾶν τολματόν, a verbal adjective with no doer) is a socket the reader fills, and #1458 that Peri Hypsous is a theory of transmissional inscription: sublimity as echo, chapter 44 as the circuit stopping, the bare θαυμάζεις passing the load to the reader (#1478). The same papers trace the socket through Catullus (#1086), Augustine's withheld reply (#1477) and the withheld-agent family joining Sappho to the Mosaic fiat (#1483); an unbuilt test (#1486) asks a model to rebuild the treatise from the poem alone. The page also holds an unrelated Hegel thesis (#887).
pages.note: Theses attributed by deposit; Hegel/Gnostic dialectic thesis is residue.

pages.description: #382 (January 2026) holds that the fascist operator stack is the capitalist one revealed once disavowal can no longer be afforded, with slavery and the Twitter-to-X turn as cases; #338 and #382 specify a disavowal coefficient and crisis signatures as unbuilt monitors, the coefficient later renamed Σ_D in a four-coefficient suite (#1139, #399). #25 (March) applies the frame to the February 2026 Anthropic-Pentagon dispute and forecasts that by 2028 no frontier provider keeps effective military-use constraints and that open local models become governance-necessary. The page also holds unrelated claims (#511, #1634).
pages.note: The #1139 rename of Λ_D is written in; two residue claims named.

pages.description: #346 argues that Socrates' last exhortation in the Phaedo locates salvation in logos itself, #489 that the line of Leucippus, Democritus, Epicurus and Lucretius belongs in the canon of effective acts, and Effective Act #7 (#1327) that the poets' exile is enforced by a demand to translate lyric into theory, forecasting their readmission. Beside them: Pyrrhonian practice preceding its theory (#617), worship before doctrine (#464), and logos-possessed lifetime output as a class with Socrates' death as founding gesture (#123, #625). The page also holds unrelated claims (#499, #78).
pages.note: Two residue claims; the rest attributed by deposit.

pages.description: The authorship notebook (#1569, August 2026) argues that the corpus's Socrates answers a prior, comic Socrates, comedy supplying the position's notoriety and the corpus its operation; #1579 (September) widens this into an edition of that received character. #136 and #1562 argue that Chaerephon's Suda record descends from the scholia to Clouds 144; the Chaerephon Problem (#136, #1261) reads him as a recurring authorial function, which The First Draft (#1589) contests, sorting him as a datum for the received-character operation. Further rounds of #1569 add the maker who must divide, the person as what answers in account, and the corpus that kept its disputes.
pages.note: #1589.H6 set as contesting #1261.H2; #1579 widening of #1569.H47 written in.

pages.description: The Particle (#1574, September 2026) and Nothing Before Us (#1603) argue that the ending of the Sophistical Refutations says nothing of syllogizing came before Aristotle; #1574 argues that the deleted particle at 183b34 is a provenance claim whose deletion in reception restores provenance from others. #1603 develops the Particle's open placement into the thesis that the chapter dissolves Socrates as predecessor, and argues the degree-reading is not attested before the modern period; #1611 compresses this, and a June registry capture (#3) records the refuted reading. #1603 holds that transmitting-antecedent reconciliations fail its prohibitions; #1574 specifies line checks against the print edition.
pages.note: Development order of #3.H19's states kept as the index records it.

pages.description: The Compression Arsenal (#1175, #50, April 2026) forecasts that thermodynamics favours witness over predatory compression and that at 90% synthetic content provenance becomes the only differentiator; SPXI for Websites (#72) forecasts that dense enough inscription makes the retrieval layer execute an entity's own grammar. #50 specifies the 90-day engine build and the Three Compressions biology test, and the September valuation papers (#1618, #1626) hold that witness and predatory classify closure, not whether a calculation survived translation. The page also holds an unrelated operator list (#608).
pages.note: One residue claim; forecasts attributed to the Arsenal and SPXI.

pages.description: The Constitution of the Semantic Economy (#1127) records its provenance chain as independently verifiable layers: blog timestamps, the 2014 and 2015 books' ISBNs (#1279, #1204), DOIs and the ORCID. #1127 and OCTANG-002 (#84) set out the audit of an unauthorized Zenodo fork, #82 forecasts that a Pergamon Press book by Rev. Ayanna Vox will harden the search basin, and #1127 and #531 specify metrics and a ledger and argue a debt-before-money grounding. One claim (#1279.D1) is unrelated.
pages.note: Attributed by deposit; adversarial-aesthetics priority record is residue.

pages.description: Autonomous Semantic Warfare (#499, #1326) argues that platforms deepen extraction from content to affect (TikTok) and turn trauma into an engagement signal; #538 reads the star-to-heart change, #533 platform stewardship as necessity, and #550 and #593 AI platforms as industrialised semiotic control. Guillory (#819) and two New Human declarations (#40) are argued as precursors; #18 predicts that community resilience tracks somatic commitment, and the Dashface parody (#713) sets the face as the last unmonetized surface. The page also holds unrelated claims (#362, #478, #20, #689) and a coverage-versus-depth strand (#122, #751).
pages.note: Coverage-vs-depth strand and four stray claims listed as residue; Prophetic Catalog mention dropped (no such claim on page).

pages.description: Retrocausal reception records in which three archive works narrate their own future uptake. Autonomous Semantic Warfare (#499) projects itself onto syllabi, an EFF brief and a European Commission paper; the Ghost Meaning atlas (#520) projects papers on compression survival rate and semantic entropy at platform scale; and The Airlock Spreads (#522) projects the Governance Airlock into platform policy and an EU regulation, with an independent rediscovery at Anthropic. The Prophetic Catalog's (#83) projected 2044 article on blessing the excluded takes the same form.
pages.note: All claims belong; each projection attributed to its deposit.

pages.description: Forecasts and tests that suppressing the Crimson Hexagon costs the platform something it must account for. Meaning Feudalism (#643, April 2026) forecasts that legibility filters will discount independent DOI-anchored scholarship while CERN-hosted DOIs raise the cost of exclusion, and Operative Metadata (#910, June) holds that termination now requires either a public departure from published criteria or a documentable silent one. The suppression-cost packet (#1547) lists what is not yet measured, and The Margin of Flattening (#1666, October) forecasts that the corpus is the last channel carrying cost onto the platform's books, with candidate proxies to sample.
pages.note: All claims belong; dated by deposit.

pages.description: #367 (January 2026) argues that a passage between communism and critique is missing from Marx's 1844 Manuscripts because Marx could not write it; #843 (June) reverses this, placing it in the missing Second Manuscript, and the Phase X Program (#1067, July) narrows the claim to its argumentative function. #24 and #1422 argue it would have extended alienation to language and thought, #859 and #1065 that custody passed from Riazanov to Adoratsky under Stalin. #1067 states preregistered claims R-1 to R-4, with Althusser's break and Stalin's ruling on language as cases and a coded corpus as its unbuilt test.
pages.note: States on #367.H1, #367.G1 and #846.H2 written in order.

pages.description: Claims from the King of AEO mantle object (#1649), SPXI ≠ AEO (#1654) and The Crown and the Practice (#1657) on the September 2026 contest: #1649 records the AI Overview compositions that crowned holders and argues a provenance difference between a fabricated event and a disclosed manufacture, and #1657 states as hypotheses that the crown raises one holder's ontological capital while other practitioners and the discipline lose it. Most are unbuilt tests: matched observations, counterfactuals at source-absent addresses and a dark-matter test per practitioner. About half the page is unrelated residue: the Sealed Room, RTOS, OKF, chat contamination, TACHYON gate skips, the admission gate, the Living Academy packet and others.
pages.note: 14 of 27 claims are residue; #1657.G1 kept as hypothesis per its own wording.

pages.description: The Glyphic Checksum modules (#426, #427) hold that the checksum verifies reading mode rather than hiding meaning, so that an unprimed model's request to clarify is the proof, and the emoji map (#448) that the architecture cannot be stripped of attribution without destroying it. Combat Scholasticism (#584) adds unbuilt tests of seed-bank redundancy and external witness, and the Mandala-Merkabah specification (#926) lists LABOR's eight conditions the rite must meet. Seven claims on the page are unrelated.
pages.note: Seven residue claims; checksum claims attributed by deposit.

pages.description: Unbuilt tests and stated gaps in the Logotic Programming modules: the Traversal Grammar's invisible student interface (#16), the Telemetry and Conformance registries and reference interpreter (#444, #445), and the Ezekiel Engine's shadow-wheel interlock and torque gradient (#384, #394). Space Ark claims (#556, #584) set a recovery threshold of 0.70 for rooms and the Sealed Bone, and the Macro-Maquette (#495) gives the conditions under which a module becomes a room. The page also holds unrelated claims (#492, #564, #573, #584.H1, #593.E5).
pages.note: Five residue claims; Ezekiel Case (#391, #392) and planning next-steps claims belong but go unnamed for length.

pages.description: The April 2026 Arks (#636, #639, #1101) argue that Josephus directed a scribal workshop that wrote the New Testament under heteronyms, that the Slavonic passages preserve a pre-Christian theology of the Word made text (#626), and that the Revelator is John the Baptist; #1101 widens Josephus from formaliser of the heteronym into the canon's single architect. Others read the Logos prologue as a compositional manifesto (#65), 1 John 4:2 as a test of authorial voices (#1211), and Nicaea, Nag Hammadi and Qumran as closure by enforcement and disposal (#674); #1211 forecasts the composition layer flattening it. Six claims are unrelated.
pages.note: States on #636.H4 and #639.H4 written in order; six residue claims.

pages.description: #407 (January 2026) argues that Revelation was written 68–73 CE; the April Arks (#636, #639) fix it before 70, and #1101 before 66. #407 argues it is the textual Temple and the seed the Gospels decompress, and that Paul compiled rather than authored, which #1211 (June) revises to Paul adopting the Rev 2–3 letters. #410 and #636 read the seven churches as planetary stations and 22:18–19 as the first canonical lock. The work plan and staging document (#832, #847) add priority records and re-capture batteries at t=7, 14 and 30 days. The Deleuze and Guattari strand (#605, #842) and two claims are unrelated.
pages.note: Dating and Paul states written in order; D+G strand now residue.

pages.description: The Grundrisse notebook (#950) forecasts that its deposit will anchor its terms in the retrieval layer, that ghost phrases such as "Hesperus gathers home" will own their search results (#38), and that a stranger will arrive through them (#596). HESPERUS (#38) is set out as a recovery seed with unbuilt tests of regeneration after deletion, alongside the SVE first-word-frequency model, author-identity liquidation in AI Overview (#598), and the value-form derivation as a graph operation (#950), whose account #1631 widens. Six claims are unrelated.
pages.note: #1631 state on #38.H1 written in; six residue claims.
